acceptanceCriteria: Specify a stable canonical CEM1.0 profile with task and provider-neutral test references, closed feature negotiation and frozen source-content-free and authority boundaries; record numbered requirements and rollback.

Implement prepare/cite/mark/verify/status/report, OCM/frontier/LRF/proof-review/MCP/portable consumer compatibility and deterministic migration without changing frozen 0.x bytes or silently accepting unsupported witnesses.
Portable schemas, adversarial exact vectors and consumer parity are retained under correct licenses, along with independent review and versioned rollback.
body:
Owner-authorized parallel child of V1-0591. Owner scope amendment 2026-10-01: "I want to get CEM to v1.0 for the main v1.0 release"; "we are supposted to be supporting all the main test runners for all the languages we support"; "work on all these in parallell". Usage credits explicitly authorized. This is the release target and execution-coverage requirement, not a promotion receipt. Existing research V1-0573 and prototype V1-0575 remain open with their original evidence obligations. Current public source has eight affected-language adapters and sixteen candidate analyzer families; runner execution and test discovery must be audited separately. Main-runner inventory must include every existing registered runner plus primary frameworks for each supported language; candidate/domain ambiguity needs explicit retained disposition rather than silent omission. Parallel lanes dynamic, native and platform use one shared experimental runner contract and one Tasks boundary lane; no default queue cutover or wire relabeling. Release promotion and merge authority remain separate.

2026-10-01 bounded experimental progress and concrete normal-repository capability gap: stable native/independently authored portable repair1 passed independent review of 532 pins, all50 complete21-key results/exits and original symlink/.GiT probes (ee98a492881c778d00299da51b7cadb04d9769d55ed9047bfd880486658d106a). This remains private prototype evidence, not source integration, default migration or independent external adoption.

The literal stable repository envelope accepts only primary .git and four exact init config shapes; ordinary origin-config checkout and linked worktree remain unsupported. Actual unmodified git init --object-format=sha256 with [extensions] before [core] refuses unsupported-repository-envelope against the private reviewed native implementation. Raw full result, Git version/argv and original config retained: /private/tmp/cem10-build/stable-next/stable-producer-prototype/ordinary-sha256-envelope/summary.json SHA6d4c0497281bb49939fa2871402abfb2a16e8e651f2b009a845a334ad482ed80; original config SHA98abe88120f0b18114dc3b1e793ba21a3f506cc133ca692b076718523968d359. Installed Core163/Tasks202 are distinct from this prototype and were not replaced. Expected stable normal-workflow support; actual explicit experimental-envelope refusal, not silently accepted evidence. No historical config was rewritten.

Deduplicated native repository-envelope search found only unrelated0339; retain this concrete missing capability under the existing all-consumer595 acceptance scope. Consumer/default staged GateA plan9dc469c355b4ae515f45f44b88c9c787c21eaa137f8327769021ba6efcbc8464 and independent review77c876a38bdd178f1f9f9a0823c4aa3796ae6d3d934998ca92a9d4c3e538e9d2 require bounded S0E native repository/process qualification before readers/mutators/OCM/frontier/completion/default switch. Corresponding portable ordinary config/order/linked-worktree behavior must qualify or remain explicit release blocker. Exact implementing filenames, public algorithms and honest full future-write native effects remain to be frozen before source admission; stages do not narrow whole-ticket authority. All original acceptance criteria remain unchanged and OPEN. Main port, source integration, all19 consumer migration, historical compatibility, external-author consumer/outcomes and explicit promotion remain unfinished.
title: CEM 1.0: freeze the portable wire and migrate every consumer
